title: Dynamic Methylation Changes in Alzheimer’s Disease-Related Genes During Mindfulness Practice – a Proof-of-Concept Study
summary: In 17 long-term meditators and 17 matched controls, researchers examined methylation at 19 CpG sites across seven genes. A month-long retreat was associated with changes at selected sites, including ABCA7 and HOXA3; some ADAM10 differences separated meditators from controls.
limitation: A small, nonrandomized blood-methylation study. It did not measure brain RNA or establish prevention or treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. Baseline average ADAM10 methylation did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction.

title: Distinct saliva DNA methylation profiles in relation to treatment outcome in youth with posttraumatic stress disorder.
authors: Ensink JBM, Henneman P, Venema A, Zantvoord JB, den Kelder RO, Mannens MMAM, Lindauer RJL.
summary: The study included 46 young people with PTSD and 41 trauma-exposed controls, aged 8–18. Saliva DNA-methylation differences associated with treatment response included C18orf63 and the stress-related CRHR2 locus.
limitation: Treatment combined evidence from EMDR and trauma-focused CBT. Saliva findings do not establish a brain-tissue effect or isolate eye movements.

title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Reduces Proinflammatory Gene Regulation But Not Systemic Inflammation Among Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Lindsay EK, Marsland AL, Cole SW, Dutcher JM, Greco CM, Wright AGC, Brown KW, Creswell JD.
summary: MBSR reduced inferred NF-κB activity relative to the active comparison programme (d=0.17; p=0.028). It did not reduce circulating IL-6 or C-reactive protein. CREB, IRF and glucocorticoid-receptor pathway differences were not statistically significant.
limitation: The gene-regulation signal was small and did not translate into a measured reduction in systemic inflammation. Pathway activity was inferred from RNA profiles.

title: Predicting psychosocial intervention response from baseline gene expression
authors: Ricon-Becker I, West TN, Fredrickson BL, Kaplan DM, Mehl MR, Raison CL, Cole SW.
design: Prediction analyses across two randomized trials
summary: Baseline CREB activity predicted selected psychological responses to compassion-based meditation in two datasets. The same relationship was not seen for mindfulness meditation.
limitation: The study concerns prediction from baseline expression rather than a demonstrated therapy-induced transcriptional mechanism. Clinical deployment requires further validation.

title: Serotonin Transporter (SLC6A4) and FK506-Binding Protein 5 (FKBP5) Genotype and Methylation Relationships with Response to Meditation in Veterans with PTSD
authors: Lee A, Thuras P, Baller J, Jiao C, Guo B, Erbes CR, Polusny MA, Liu C, Wu B, Lim KO, Bishop JR.
design: Secondary analysis of two intervention studies
summary: SLC6A4 genotype was associated with symptom improvement among veterans exposed to early-life trauma. Change in a group of nine FKBP5 methylation sites was associated with greater improvement (OR 2.8; 95% CI 1.1–7.1).
limitation: Genotype and DNA methylation were measured; this is not direct RNA-expression evidence. Associations across two meditation studies do not isolate a treatment mechanism.

title: Light damage induces inflammatory factors in mouse retina and vitreous humor
authors: Liu W, Zhu X, Ge X, Chen Y, Li DW, Gong L.
summary: Strong light exposure induced retinal inflammatory transcriptional changes. Vitreous IL-6 protein was approximately tenfold higher in the injury model.
limitation: The IL-6 fold change concerns vitreous protein. This is a harmful exposure model, not evidence for a therapeutic visual protocol.

title: Music compensates for altered gene expression in age-related cognitive disorders
authors: Gómez-Carballa A, Navarro L, Pardo-Seco J, Bello X, Pischedda S, Viz-Lasheras S, Camino-Mera A, Currás MJ, Ferreirós I, Mallah N, Rey-Vázquez S, Redondo L, Dacosta-Urbieta A, Caamaño-Viña F, Rivero-Calle I, Rodriguez-Tenreiro C, Martinón-Torres F, Salas A.
summary: A music session was associated with blood gene-expression changes in people with age-related cognitive disorders and healthy controls. Some affected pathways overlapped inversely with disease-associated expression patterns.
limitation: Before–after molecular associations and cross-dataset comparisons do not establish that music reverses dementia or changes brain gene expression.

title: Transcriptional Modulation of Stress-Related Genes in Association with Early Life Stress Exposure and Trauma-Focused Psychotherapy in Treatment-Resistant Depression Patients

authors: Rosana Carvalho Silva; Vincenzo Dattilo; Giulia Perusi; Monica Mazzelli; Elisabetta Maffioletti; Roberta Bazzanella; Marco Bortolomasi; Annamaria Cattaneo; Massimo Gennarelli; Alessandra Minelli
summary: In 21 people receiving EMDR or trauma-focused CBT for treatment-resistant depression, whole-blood NR3C1, FKBP5 and SGK1 expression varied over time. FKBP5 and SGK1 fell significantly at eight weeks; transcript levels rebounded during follow-up.

authors: Hu S, Wang Y, Han X, Dai M, Zhang Y, Ma Y, Weng S, Xiao L, Xiao L.

journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
authors: Gao AY, Link PA, Bakri SJ, Haak AJ.
design: Human retinal pigment epithelial cell-line experiment
summary: DRD2 and DRD5 were prominent receptors in ARPE-19 cells. Dopamine-receptor manipulation altered profibrotic gene expression and cellular fibrosis measures.

authors: Kaliman P, Cosín-Tomás M, Madrid A, Roque López S, Llanez-Anaya E, Papale LA, Alisch RS, Davidson RJ.
summary: A one-week programme combining mindfulness, artistic expression and EMDR group therapy studied 44 adolescent girls with multiple adverse experiences. Forty-nine DNA-methylation loci differed with intervention; SIRT5 and TRAPPC2L changes correlated with trauma measures.

title: Glial cell response to constant low light exposure in rat retina
authors: Bruera MG, Benedetto MM, Guido ME, Degano AL, Contin MA.
summary: Prolonged constant low light was followed by retinal degeneration, glial activation and increased immune-mediator expression, including IL-6 and TNF.
limitation: This is a retinal-damage model. It does not establish that ordinary visual activity produces the same changes, or that increased expression is beneficial.

title: Online, low-volume meditation does not alter immune-related biomarkers
authors: Graham B, Jin Y, Bazeley P, Husni E, Calabrese LH.
summary: The trial found no significant between-group differences in the prespecified immune-related gene set, wider RNA expression or other tested biomarkers. Stress improved earlier in the music group and later in the mindfulness group.
limitation: A small trial of brief online practice in otherwise healthy nurses. The result concerns this dose and delivery; it does not establish the absence of effects from other programmes.

title: Oxytocin pathway gene networks in the human brain
authors: Quintana DS, Rokicki J, van der Meer D, Alnæs D, Kaufmann T, Córdova-Palomera A, Dieset I, Andreassen OA, Westlye LT.
design: Human post-mortem expression mapping and co-expression analysis
quotes: ["“Three oxytocin signaling genes have been frequently implicated in human social behavior: OXT (structural gene for oxytocin), OXTR (oxytocin receptor), and CD38 (oxytocin secretion).”","“Expression of the three selected oxytocin pathway genes was enriched in subcortical and olfactory regions and there was high co-expression with several dopaminergic and muscarinic acetylcholine genes, reflecting an anatomical basis for critical gene pathway interactions.”","“The oxytocin signaling system may interact with dopaminergic and muscarinic acetylcholine signaling to modulate cognitive state processes involved in complex human behaviors.”"]
summary: Human brain expression maps showed regional enrichment of oxytocin-pathway transcripts and co-expression with dopaminergic and muscarinic acetylcholine genes. The study provides anatomical context for an OXTR-centred research programme.
limitation: Spatial co-expression is an association. This study did not test sound, vision or language interventions, Fibonacci-derived features, or causal interactions across the proposed target network.

title: Preliminary indications of the effect of a brief yoga intervention on markers of inflammation and DNA methylation in chronically stressed women
authors: K N Harkess; J Ryan; P H Delfabbro; S Cohen-Woods
design: Exploratory molecular substudy of a yoga trial
summary: An exploratory substudy in chronically stressed women reported lower methylation in a TNF region following a brief yoga intervention. Comparable regional changes were not found for IL6 or CRP, and a reduction in circulating inflammatory markers was not established.
limitation: The molecular sample contained 28 women. Its retrospective and uncontrolled longitudinal components limit causal interpretation, despite recruitment from a larger randomized trial.

authors: Bower JE, Crosswell AD, Stanton AL, Crespi CM, Winston D, Arevalo J, Ma J, Cole SW, Ganz PA.
design: Randomized controlled trial; blinding not reported
quotes: ["“A brief, mindfulness‐based intervention demonstrated preliminary short‐term efficacy in reducing stress, behavioral symptoms, and proinflammatory signaling in younger breast cancer survivors”","“women in the mindfulness group who practiced more frequently did evidence lower levels of IL‐6 at the post‐treatment assessment”","“our trial indicates that the benefits of mindfulness may extend to genomic markers of inflammation, including reductions in proinflammatory gene expression and activity of the proinflammatory transcription factor NF‐ κ B”"]

limitation: A preliminary waitlist-controlled trial in a specific survivor population. Molecular changes do not establish a reduction in cancer recurrence or progression.

title: Oxytocin receptor gene (OXTR) is related to psychological resources
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
authors: Saphire-Bernstein S, Way BM, Kim HS, Sherman DK, Taylor SE.
quotes: ["“Psychological resources—optimism, mastery, and self-esteem—buffer the deleterious effects of stress and are predictors of neurophysiological and psychological health-related outcomes. These resources have been shown to be highly heritable, yet the genetic basis for this heritability remains unknown.”","“Here, we report a link between the oxytocin receptor (OXTR) SNP rs53576 and psychological resources, such that carriers of the “A” allele have lower levels of optimism, mastery, and self-esteem, relative to G/G homozygotes.”","“OXTR was also associated with depressive symptomatology. Mediation analysis indicates that the effects of OXTR on depressive symptoms may be largely mediated by the influence of OXTR on psychological resources.”"]

title: Community singing intervention reduces maternal salivary cytokines and enhances maternal-infant cortisol synchrony in postnatal depression: biological findings from the SHAPER-PND trial

title: Preoperative binaural beats reduce remimazolam dosage and enhance safety in anesthesia induction: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Kim HC, Sohn JY, Kim MH, Kim YJ, Chang CH, Seo JH.
summary: In 72 surgical patients, 30 minutes of 1 Hz binaural beats reduced the mean remimazolam dose required for loss of consciousness from 17.7 to 15.0 mg; hypotension occurred in 6% versus 28% of participants.
limitation: A single-centre anaesthesia study with no auditory intervention in the comparison arm. EEG differences were not significant, so the proposed entrainment mechanism remains unconfirmed.

title: Surface code scaling on heavy-hex superconducting quantum processors
authors: Arian Vezvaee; Cesar Benito; Mario Morford-Oberst; Alejandro Bermudez; Daniel A. Lidar
summary: The authors combine surface-code layouts and pulse control on IBM heavy-hex processors. Increasing code size along one direction improves protection of particular logical states. Their analysis shows why both state directions and coherent noise matter when assessing error suppression.
limitation: Directional improvements do not establish general below-threshold scaling. The paper identifies further noise reduction needed for balanced scaling. It does not test Fibonacci or M9 P24 sequences.

title: The new exponential Fibonacci neighborhood as QUBO generated on a D-Wave quantum computing environment for the permutational scheduling problem
authors: Wojciech Bożejko; Mariusz Uchroński; Mieczysław Wodecki
design: Combinatorial construction and quantum-annealing computational experiment
summary: The authors construct a permutation neighbourhood with Fibonacci-number cardinality and encode it using a binary sequence of length n−1. They test a related QUBO formulation on a D-Wave system for a single-machine scheduling problem.
limitation: A compact encoding and tested scheduling results do not prove a general quantum speedup. Performance depends on the neighbourhood restriction, instance selection and hardware; appraisal here is abstract-level.

title: Theta binaural beats for pain, cognition and anxiety
summary: Across 13 RCTs, theta (4-8 Hz) binaural beats reduced pain, showed anxiety benefit mainly in procedural and chronic-pain settings, and improved episodic memory—supporting focused testing in Universal Mind's 5-8 Hz range.
limitation: Overall pain evidence was low certainty, outcomes varied, and the review does not establish PTSD efficacy or validate a complete sound layer.

title: Binaural beat stimulation as a tool to reduce preoperative anxiety in patients undergoing elective surgery and general anesthesia - results from a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Ostertag J, Zinn S, Georgii MT, Niederle MB, Pinto Campos C, Schneider G, Hayden O, Kratzer S, Kreuzer M.
summary: Preoperative binaural-beat stimulation produced a greater reduction in reported state anxiety than the control condition. The reported difference in relative anxiety change was approximately six percentage points.
limitation: The authors identified music and relaxation as plausible contributors. Alpha power did not differ between groups; the trial does not isolate a beat-specific mechanism.

authors: Madhumitha TK, Esther V, Ravishankar PL, Kalaivani, Kumar G, Rajula PB.

title: Effects of preoperative binaural beats on the propofol dose for induction of general anesthesia: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
authors: Kim YJ, Choe HW, Yoon SB, Lee H, Kim HS, Seo JH.
summary: Among 69 surgical patients, 20 minutes of 1 Hz binaural beats reduced the mean propofol dose needed to stop responding to verbal commands from 105 to 87 mg; the difference was -18 mg, with a 95% confidence interval of -32 to -5 mg.
limitation: Anxiety and frontal EEG bands did not differ significantly. This supports an anaesthetic-dose finding within the tested clinical protocol, rather than a general claim of brainwave entrainment.

title: Fibonacci-modulation-induced multiple topological Anderson insulators
authors: Ruijiang Ji; Zhihao Xu

title: Heat-rechargeable computation in DNA logic circuits and neural networks
authors: Tianqi Song; Lulu Qian
summary: Heat resets engineered DNA circuits for repeated computation. A feedforward logic circuit returns the first 16 Fibonacci-word elements from index inputs and maintains performance across 16 computation rounds with 15 resets.
limitation: The Fibonacci circuit uses a designed truth table and finite inputs. It does not autonomously generate an unbounded sequence or reveal a naturally occurring genomic computation.

title: Psychological Interventions for Pediatric Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
authors: Hoppen TH, Wessarges L, Jehn M, Mutz J, Kip A, Schlechter P, Meiser-Stedman R, Morina N.
summary: Across 70 pediatric PTSD trials involving 5,528 participants, EMDR reduced symptoms relative to passive controls at treatment end (g = 0.86). Trauma-focused CBT had the most consistent evidence across time points.
limitation: The 70 trials cover several therapies, not EMDR alone. Longer-term EMDR data remain limited; included ages extend to 19.

authors: Zlatko K. Minev; Khadijeh Najafi; Swarnadeep Majumder; Juven Wang; Ady Stern; Eun-Ah Kim; Chao-Ming Jian; Guanyu Zhu
summary: The authors construct Fibonacci string-net states with a dynamical preparation method, measure and braid anyons, and estimate chromatic polynomials for several graphs using quantum samples.

summary: Of 151 women randomised after a traumatic birth, 143 entered the reported intention-to-treat analysis. title: Brain wave modulation and EEG power changes during auditory beats stimulation
authors: Dos Anjos T, Di Rienzo F, Benoit CE, Daligault S, Guillot A.
summary: In 28 healthy participants, four minutes of isochronic-derived stimulation produced greater gamma-band EEG power changes than gamma binaural beats and white noise, alongside a distinct time-related alpha response.
limitation: The stimulus alternated audible frequencies rather than using a conventional fixed-carrier isochronic tone and did not test Universal Mind's exact protocol. It measured short-term EEG responses, not a clinical outcome.

title: Enhancing image security via chaotic maps, Fibonacci, Tribonacci transformations, and DWT diffusion: a robust data encryption approach
authors: Mohammad Mazyad Hazzazi; Mujeeb Ur Rehman; Arslan Shafique; Amer Aljaedi; Zaid Bassfar; Aminu Bello Usman
summary: The proposed grayscale-image encryption pipeline combines chaotic keys, Fibonacci pixel permutation, Tribonacci transformations, bit-plane operations and wavelet-based diffusion. The paper reports statistical and timing tests.
limitation: Entropy, pixel correlation and timing tests do not alone establish cryptographic security. The multi-component pipeline also prevents attributing its reported performance solely to Fibonacci transforms.

title: Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy compared to usual treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults with psychosis in forensic settings: Randomized controlled trial.
journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
authors: Every-Palmer S, Flewett T, Dean S, Hansby O, Freeland A, Weatherall M, Bell E.
summary: In 24 forensic patients with psychosis and PTSD, blinded assessments favoured EMDR over routine-care waitlist for clinician-rated PTSD symptoms. The estimated difference averaged across follow-ups was 11.4 points, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.3 to 21.4.
limitation: Recruitment was curtailed by pandemic restrictions, leaving a small sample. Psychotic symptoms and adverse events did not differ significantly, so effectiveness claims remain specific to the measured PTSD outcomes.

authors: Zhi Li; Latham Boyle
summary: Li and Boyle construct quantum error-correcting codes from Penrose tilings and variants based on Ammann–Beenker and Fibonacci tilings. Their construction connects nonperiodic geometric structure with the ability to recover information after local errors or erasures.

title: Light disrupts social memory via a retina-to-supraoptic nucleus circuit
authors: Huang YF, Liao PY, Yu JH, Chen SK.
summary: Acute light exposure impaired social-recognition memory through a retinal pathway that inhibited supraoptic oxytocin neurons. Experimental activation of these neurons altered the behavioural response.
limitation: Neural activity and behavioural changes are separate from OXTR gene expression. The animal circuit findings do not validate a human visual intervention.

title: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial of Transcendental Meditation as Treatment for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder in Veterans.
authors: Bellehsen M, Stoycheva V, Cohen BH, Nidich S.
summary: In 40 veterans with PTSD, Transcendental Meditation reduced clinician-rated symptoms more than usual care over 12 weeks. Half of the meditation group no longer met PTSD criteria, compared with 10% of controls.
limitation: A small pilot with usual-care comparison. Anger and quality of life did not differ significantly; this does not establish equivalence to trauma-focused psychotherapy.

title: Dynamical topological phase realized in a trapped-ion quantum simulator
authors: Philipp T. Dumitrescu; Justin G. Bohnet; John P. Gaebler; Aaron Hankin; David Hayes; Ajesh Kumar; Brian Neyenhuis; Romain Vasseur; Andrew C. Potter
summary: A quasiperiodic Fibonacci drive creates a dynamical topological phase in a ten-qubit trapped-ion chain. Edge-qubit behaviour exhibits protection against specified control imperfections relative to a periodic-drive comparison.
limitation: The result concerns a finite quantum simulator and particular dynamics. It does not demonstrate general-purpose fault tolerance; the present appraisal covers the abstract and accessible extended-data descriptions.

authors: Taylor H, Cavanagh K, Field AP, Strauss C.
summary: In 2,182 NHS staff, a digital mindfulness app produced a small but statistically significant reduction in stress relative to an active digital control over 4.5 months, with additional benefits on several wellbeing measures.

title: Binaural Beats Reduce Postoperative Morphine Consumption in Older adults After Total Knee Replacement Surgery.
journal: Alternative therapies in health and medicine
authors: Tani A, Vagheggini G, Moretti F, Del Colombo V, Lehle J, Campana S, Labate A, Tomaiuolo F.

authors: Kazuaki Amikura; Hiroshi Ito; Miho S. Kitazawa
design: Plant morphology measurements and mathematical model
summary: Rose stems show a non-random distribution of prickles relative to spiral leaf phyllotaxis. A diffusion-based inhibition model reproduces the measured pattern and selected patterns in other plants.
limitation: The primary measurements cover nine shoots of one rose cultivar. The model assumes a patterning process; the responsible inhibitory factors and broader applicability remain unresolved.

title: Dynamically Generated Logical Qubits
authors: Matthew B. Hastings; Jeongwan Haah
summary: Hastings and Haah construct a honeycomb code in which a repeating schedule of two-qubit measurements creates logical qubits. Information protection comes from the code and measurement sequence acting together on the lattice.
limitation: The paper does not show that a passive hexagon alone protects information. Implementing this code requires the specified measurements and decoding; the current Aquila workflow does not implement that procedure.

title: Explosive Fibonacci-sequence growth into unusual sector-face morphology in poly(l-lactic acid) crystallized with polymeric diluents
authors: Graecia Lugito; Selvaraj Nagarajan; Eamor M. Woo
summary: In diluted poly(l-lactic acid) crystals, microscopy reveals branching lamellar sectors whose branch counts grow approximately along a Fibonacci sequence. Thermal and scattering measurements characterize the resulting structures.
limitation: The authors describe approximate counts and acknowledge difficulty distinguishing branches. The polymers and crystallization conditions are specific; this is not evidence for a universal exact growth law.

title: Gamification Use and Design in Popular Health and Fitness Mobile Applications
journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
authors: Cotton V, Patel MS.
quotes: ["“Gamification was commonly used by popular health and fitness mobile applications, but none used the specified behavioral economic principles to design rewards or points. Mobile applications could potentially improve their use if their design better leveraged principles from behavioral economic”","“Use of behavioral economic principles focused on designing rewards or points using loss aversion (allocated upfront and could be lost), variable reinforcement (not allocated constantly), and probability inflation (using drawings or lottery designs).”","“The top 50 rankes free health and fitness apps were downloaded from the App Store by Apple. Gamification was used by 64% of mobile applications. Most applications that included gamification (97%) targeted behaviors related to physical activity and weight loss. Applications focused on other areas such as reproductive health, meditation, and sleep used gamification less often (11%). Game elements used most commonly included goal setting (78%), social influences (78%), and challenges (63%), while less common elements included points (6%) and levels (3%). No applications incorporated behavioral economics principles specified in the study.”"]

title: A mindfulness-based intervention to increase resilience to stress in university students (the Mindful Student Study): a pragmatic randomised controlled trial.
authors: Galante J, Dufour G, Vainre M, Wagner AP, Stochl J, Benton A, Lathia N, Howarth E, Jones PB.
design: Single-blind randomized controlled trial (outcome assessors blinded)
summary: In the 616-student Mindful Student Study, an eight-week course reduced exam-period psychological distress relative to usual support. The adjusted difference was -0.14 CORE-OM points, with a 95% confidence interval of -0.22 to -0.06.
limitation: Only 74% completed the exam-period outcome, and 59% of assigned students attended at least half the course. Participants knew allocation and the comparator did not match instructor attention.

title: Fractional Transport of Photons in Deterministic Aperiodic Structures
authors: Luca Dal Negro; Sandeep Inampudi
design: Numerical wave transport and analytical fractional-dynamics modelling
summary: Transfer-matrix simulations compare photon propagation in deterministic aperiodic structures. Fibonacci and Thue–Morse stacks exhibit anomalous power-law transport, while Rudin–Shapiro structures exhibit a distinct logarithmic regime.
limitation: These are modelled transport regimes under specified optical assumptions. The logarithmic result is associated with Rudin–Shapiro structures, not a finding unique to Fibonacci sequences.

title: Mindfulness meditation and improvement in sleep quality and daytime impairment among older adults with sleep disturbances: a randomized clinical trial.
authors: Black DS, O'Reilly GA, Olmstead R, Breen EC, Irwin MR.
summary: In 49 older adults with sleep disturbance, mindful-awareness training improved Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores by 1.8 points more than structured sleep-hygiene education, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.6 to 2.9.
limitation: The trial was small and measured immediate post-treatment effects. Inflammatory NF-kappaB measures did not differ between groups, so the sleep benefit does not establish that molecular pathway as its cause.

title: A healthy heart is not a metronome: an integrative review of the heart's anatomy and heart rate variability
authors: Shaffer F, McCraty R, Zerr CL.
quotes: ["“Physiological coherence is used broadly and includes all of the specific approaches for quantifying the various types of coherence measures, such as cross-coherence (frequency entrainment between respiration, BP, and heart rhythms), or synchronization among systems (e.g., synchronization between various EEG rhythms and the cardiac cycle), auto-coherence (stability of a single waveform such as respiration or HRV patterns), and system resonance.”","“A coherent heart rhythm is defined as a relatively harmonic (sine-wave-like) signal with a very narrow, high-amplitude peak in the LF region of the HRV power spectrum with no major peaks in the VLF or HF regions. Coherence is assessed by identifying the maximum peak in the 0.04–0.26 Hz range of the HRV power spectrum, calculating the integral in a window 0.030 Hz wide, centered on the highest peak in that region, and then calculating the total power of the entire spectrum. The coherence ratio is formulated as: (Peak Power/[Total Power – Peak Power])”","“With practice, people can learn to breathe at their cardiovascular system's resonance frequency. This aligns the three oscillators (baroreflex, HR, and BP) at that frequency and moves the peak frequency from the HF range (≈0.2 Hz) to the LF range (≈0.1 Hz). Breathing at the resonance frequency more than doubles the energy in the LF band (0.04–0.15 Hz). This corresponds to the Institute of HeartMath's heart rhythm coherence, which is associated with a “narrow, high-amplitude, easily visualized peak” from 0.09 to 0.14 Hz”","“The resonance frequency model uses the mechanism of slow breathing at an individual’s resonance frequency, while the psychological coherence model adds and emphasizes the importance of the pattern and stability of vagal afferent traffic as important components of emotional self-regulation. Both approaches have been associated with increased overall HRV over time.”","“There is agreement that the concept of “coherence” in the heart rate signal is observed as a peak in the HRV power spectrum around 0.1 Hz, which reflects resonance frequency of breathing and resonance in the baroreflex. The authors’ “psychophysiological coherence model” advocates biofeedback training that actually creates a maximum of HRV variability at this virtual single frequency.”","“It is known that the power spectrum distribution of normal fluctuations in a healthy heart follows an 1/f pattern, characteristic of fractal signals. So, this leads us to juxtapose Coherence and simplicity vs fractals and complexity.”"]

authors: Bowen S, Witkiewitz K, Clifasefi SL, Grow J, Chawla N, Hsu SH, Carroll HA, Harrop E, Collins SE, Lustyk MK, Larimer ME.
summary: In 286 adults completing substance-use treatment, mindfulness-based relapse prevention reduced substance-use days and heavy drinking at 12 months relative to standard relapse prevention and usual aftercare.

title: Dancing with Refugees - Expressing Feelings and Experiences
quotes: ["“Through dance, I can express experiences that I would not be able to verbalize in any other way. The possibility of using dance to say something about oneself, one’s own feelings and views is not to be found in traditional dance, which was what I learnt first. Rather, it is contemporary dance that makes that possible.”","“But in the workshops I feel it is important to start with tradition in order to show the participants that dance has something to do with them. It is part of their culture and can also become a means through which they can express themselves.”","“Dancing together brings them into the present, it creates a specific moment. That may be the starting point for actively shaping the future. Through reviving the culture the refugees feel they have lost, we lead them to a new way of dealing with it. It is as if we were opening up the possibility of a retrospective view, but one that focuses on what was beautiful and not on the suffering.”"]
